page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no margin notes; below the text a signature mark at the foot right.

main_text.l: egent. Cæterum ideo non putrescit ignis
Aristoteli, quòd sit forma aliorum elemen-
torum, quæ quidē ei materia sint: aut quia
humido putredinis subiecto caret. Hac de
causa terra simplex, sinceraq; putrescere ne-
quit. Quapropter possunt putrescere sola
aqua & aër: quando uidelicet hic non per-
flatur, illa uero non fluit. Tunc enim aliorū
elementorum permistione, & externi calo-
ris interuentu quodammodo putrescunt,
& corrumpuntur. Plantæ & animalia, licet
primùm corrumpetur diffolutione ficci ab
humido, uti & formæ à materia: tamen tan-
dem putrescūt: quoniam putredo est finis
omnis, quæ natura constituuntur. Propte-
re a eam rectè opponit Aristotel. lib. 4. me-
teo. cap. 1. simplici generationi, quæ natura
lis est & propria. Postremò putrescunt hu-
mores in animalium corporibus prohibi-
ta transpiratione. Quòd putredinis genus
duplex constituit, Galenus libro primo de
Differetiis febrium. Prius autem est, in quo
natura uincit, quale in abscessibus apparet
& est in febribus, quæ per se lethales non
sunt. Huiusmodi putredo in abscessibus
suppuratio dicitur, & imperfecta putredo;
quoniam concoctioni coniuncta est. Poste rius

page.notes: Text is faint in places; the catchword-like "rius" at the foot is the start of the printed word "posterius" split by the signature line, rendered as printed. Doubtful readings: "Proptere a" may be a line-break artefact for "Proptereā"; "tandem" in "tamen tandem" is read from a faint word; "Quòd" and "quæ quidē" are as printed. Long s is plain s throughout. The phrase "Poste rius" is printed as a line-end split and the second part appears at the foot beside the signature.
